chunks: And by this chain, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The zakat of knowledge is that you teach it to the servants of God.

key_terms.زكاة العلم: The zakat (purifying due/obligatory portion) of knowledge — using the almsgiving metaphor for intellectual transmission
key_terms.عباد الله: Servants/worshippers of God — all believers to whom knowledge must be disseminated

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat of knowledge in Islam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) uses the concept of zakat — the obligatory purifying alms normally applied to wealth — as a metaphor for knowledge: just as wealth must be shared to be spiritually purified, knowledge must be taught and disseminated. This teaching reflects the Imam's emphasis on the social responsibility of those who possess religious knowledge. In the early Islamic scholarly milieu, this hadith called scholars to share their learning freely rather than hoarding it, framing teaching as a religious duty (like zakat) rather than merely a virtuous act.
